tip: The receiver goes in the dative: маме (mame = to mom). The gift цветы (tsvety = flowers) stays the direct object.
After стал (stal = became), the new role goes in the instrumental: известным врачом (izvestnym vrachom = a famous doctor).
The verb гордимся (gordimsya = we are proud) takes the instrumental with no preposition: нашими детьми (nashimi det'mi = our children).
с (s = with) takes the instrumental: с грибами (s gribami = with mushrooms), naming what the soup is made with.
о (o = about) takes the prepositional case: о своём детстве (o svoyom detstve = about her childhood).
требует (trebuyet = requires) takes the genitive, not the accusative: большого терпения (bol'shogo terpeniya = great patience).
This masculine noun takes a stressed -у for location: в углу (v uglu = in the corner), not the usual -е ending.
за (za = behind) takes the instrumental for a static location: за забором (za zaborom = behind the fence).
With no stated subject, the plural verb подарили (podarili = they gave) reads as a passive, was given, the normal Russian pattern.
понравилась (ponravilas', feminine) agrees with презентация (prezentatsiya = presentation), the thing liked, not with коллегам (kollegam = colleagues).
The tool used takes the instrumental with no preposition: ложкой (lozhkoy = with a spoon).
известна (izvestna = is known) puts the person who knows in the dative: мне (mne = to me), literally the problem is known to me.
Here с (s = with) takes the genitive, not the instrumental: с чашки (s chashki = with a cup), meaning starting from.
даётся (dayotsya = comes easily) puts the person in the dative: ей (yey = to her); математика (matematika = maths) stays the subject.
интересуется (interesuyetsya = is interested) takes the instrumental: русской историей (russkoy istoriyey = in Russian history).
